explanation: Begin with the empty subset. For each value, retain every old subset and add one copy containing the new value.
spaceComplexity: O(n · 2^n) output; O(n) for each temporary subset copy.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Initially the output is the power set of an empty prefix. When a new value arrives, each subset of the larger prefix either excludes it and is already present, or includes it and is formed uniquely by adding it to one old subset. Thus every subset appears exactly once after all values are processed.
walkthrough: For input [6,9], begin with [[]]. Processing 6 adds [6]. Processing 9 copies the two old subsets and adds 9, yielding [9] and [6,9]. The result is [[],[6],[9],[6,9]], in any accepted subset order.
edgeCases: An empty set returns a list containing the empty subset.
The input is a set; distinct values avoid duplicate subset identities.
Copies keep previously generated subsets unchanged.
